# 2-Week Hotel Maintenance Programme

**Client:** 32F, intermediate, mid-hypertrophy block
**Equipment:** Yoga mat, doorway pull-up bar
**Goal:** Maintain muscle mass and movement quality during travel; return ready to resume Week 7 loading without deconditioning

## Programming Rationale

Research on detraining (Bickel, Cross & Bamman 2011; Ogasawara et al. 2013) shows trained individuals can maintain muscle mass for 2–3 weeks on as little as 1/3 of normal training volume, *provided intensity proximity to failure is preserved*. With bodyweight-only training, the lever to preserve stimulus is **mechanical tension via tempo, unilateral variants, pauses, and proximity to failure (RIR 0–2)**. We'll run 4 sessions per week — enough frequency to hit each muscle group 2x — keeping sessions short (35–45 min) to suit travel fatigue and hotel constraints.

Two upper / two lower split, with a mobility flow on off days.

---

## Weekly Structure (Both Weeks)

- **Day 1:** Upper Push/Pull A
- **Day 2:** Lower A
- **Day 3:** Mobility flow + core (20 min, optional)
- **Day 4:** Upper Push/Pull B
- **Day 5:** Lower B
- **Day 6 & 7:** Rest or walking

Days can flex around her travel schedule — just keep at least one rest day between same-pattern sessions.

---

## WEEK 1 — Grooving the Stimulus

### Day 1 — Upper A

| Exercise | Sets x Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Pull-ups | 4 x AMRAP (stop 1 RIR) | If >10, add 3-sec eccentric |
| Pike push-ups (feet on bed) | 3 x 8–12 | Shoulder-dominant |
| Archer push-ups | 3 x 6–8 per side | Or assisted one-arm progression |
| Inverted rows under desk/table (if sturdy) OR scapular pulls | 3 x 10–12 | |
| Hollow body hold | 3 x 30 sec | |

### Day 2 — Lower A

| Exercise | Sets x Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Bulgarian split squat (rear foot on chair) | 4 x 10–12/leg | 3-sec descent, hold suitcase if available for load |
| Single-leg Romanian deadlift | 3 x 10/leg | Slow, balance-focused |
| Cossack squat | 3 x 8/side | |
| Glute bridge march | 3 x 10/side | |
| Copenhagen plank (short lever ok) | 2 x 20 sec/side | Adductor maintenance |

### Day 3 — Mobility + Core (optional)

10-min cat-cow → world's greatest stretch → 90/90 flow → thoracic openers. Finish with hollow hold 3x30s and side plank 2x30s/side.

### Day 4 — Upper B

| Exercise | Sets x Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Chin-ups (supinated) | 4 x AMRAP (1 RIR) | Biceps emphasis |
| Push-ups (standard, 2-sec pause at bottom) | 4 x 12–15 | |
| Pseudo planche push-ups | 3 x 6–8 | Hands by hips, lean forward |
| Towel face pulls (anchor in door hinge) | 3 x 15 | Rear delt/upper back |
| Side plank reach-through | 3 x 8/side | |

### Day 5 — Lower B

| Exercise | Sets x Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Pistol squat progression (box/bed assisted) | 4 x 6–8/leg | |
| Reverse lunge | 3 x 10/leg | Slow, controlled |
| Nordic curl negatives (anchor feet under bed) | 3 x 4–6 | Hamstring stimulus is hard bodyweight — this is the key lift |
| Single-leg glute bridge | 3 x 12/leg | 2-sec hold at top |
| Calf raise off stair/step | 4 x 15–20 | Single-leg if able |

---

## WEEK 2 — Push Intensity, Maintain Volume

Same template, but increase difficulty rather than reps:
- Push-up tempos slow to 4-sec eccentric, 1-sec pause
- Pull-ups: add 5-sec hold at top on final rep of each set
- Bulgarian split squats: 1.5-rep style (full rep + half rep = 1)
- Nordic negatives: aim for 6-sec descent
- Pistols: reduce assistance (lower box, fingertip support only)

Hit each set within 1 RIR. Volume stays the same; **intensity proximity creeps up.** This is what protects muscle without requiring loaded equipment.

---

## Recovery & Nutrition Notes

- **Protein:** Hold her usual intake (~1.6–2.0 g/kg). Travel often means under-eating protein — coach her to anchor every meal with a palm-sized portion (eggs at breakfast, chicken/fish at lunch/dinner, Greek yogurt or jerky snacks).
- **Calories:** Slight maintenance is fine; do not let her drift into a deficit during this block as it accelerates muscle loss in a low-stimulus environment.
- **Sleep:** Flag the importance of this — travel disrupts it most. Suggest blackout mask, melatonin if crossing time zones.
- **Steps:** Aim 8–10k/day. Easy aerobic work supports recovery and offsets sedentary travel days.
- **Hydration:** +500ml/day above normal if flying.

---

## Returning to Week 7

When she's back, deload the first session by ~10% off her Week 6 working loads, then resume normal Week 7 progression. She shouldn't have lost meaningful strength or size — expect 1 session of "feeling it out" and she's back on track.

Want me to build out the Week 7–12 return block next?

Good call — programming for the lowest common denominator means she never has to improvise or skip a session. The plan above stays as-is.

That said, here's how to **opportunistically use dumbbells if they appear**, without rewriting the programme:

## "If Dumbbells Are Available" Add-Ons

Treat them as bonus load, not a replacement. Slot them into the existing session — same exercises, same set/rep targets, same RIR — just add load where it makes the movement harder.

### Upper Days

- **Pull-ups / chin-ups:** Hold a light DB between feet if AMRAP sets exceed 12 reps
- **Push-up variants:** Skip the DBs here — tempo and leverage are doing the work
- **Add at the end (3 sets each, 1 RIR):**
  - DB lateral raise 3 x 12–15 — almost any weight works; side delts are hard to hit bodyweight
  - DB curl or hammer curl 3 x 10–12 — bonus arm volume
  - DB overhead tricep extension 3 x 10–12

These three are the highest-yield additions because they target muscles bodyweight training underloads (side delts, biceps in non-pulling context, triceps long head).

### Lower Days

- **Bulgarian split squats:** Hold DBs at sides — best single use of dumbbells in the whole plan
- **Single-leg RDL:** Hold DB in opposite hand
- **Reverse lunges:** Goblet or suitcase carry style
- **Glute bridges:** DB on hips

### Rules of Engagement

1. **Don't chase load.** If she's got 5kg DBs, that's fine — keep proximity to failure, don't add reps beyond the prescribed range to compensate.
2. **Don't add new exercises she'd have to drop next day.** Whatever loaded work she does Monday, she should be able to repeat Thursday — gym access permitting or not.
3. **If the gym has them two days running, great. If it disappears, the bodyweight plan still hits the target stimulus.**

This way the dumbbells become a small upside — particularly for side delts and biceps, which are the two clearest "holes" in a pure bodyweight maintenance block — without the programme depending on them.

Ready to map out the Week 7–12 return block whenever you are.

# Cardio Finishers — 15 min, Post-Session

These bolt onto the end of each of the 4 lifting sessions. Mobility day stays as-is (or she can add an easy Zone 2 walk instead).

**Programming logic:** She's in a hypertrophy block, so finishers stay **low-impact on recovery** — meaning we avoid hammering the same muscle groups she just trained, and we keep total weekly hard conditioning to ~2 sessions. The other two are moderate intent. This gives her the conditioning hit she enjoys without bleeding into lifting recovery or eating into the muscle she's trying to maintain.

Bodyweight-only, no equipment needed beyond the mat.

---

## Day 1 (Upper A) — Lower-Body Intervals (Moderate)

Lower body is fresh, so we use it. EMOM style — Every Minute On the Minute for 15 minutes:

- **Min 1:** 20 jump squats (or squat-to-stand if downstairs neighbours)
- **Min 2:** 30-sec high knees
- **Min 3:** 15 reverse lunges (alternating)

Repeat 5 rounds. Rest is whatever's left in the minute. Target: finish each minute with 15–20 sec rest. If she's getting <10 sec, scale reps down.

---

## Day 2 (Lower A) — Upper/Core Circuit (Moderate)

Legs are cooked, so we go upper and core. 40 sec work / 20 sec rest, 3 rounds:

1. Push-up to shoulder tap
2. Mountain climbers
3. Plank up-downs
4. Bear crawl in place (or forward/back if space)
5. Hollow rocks

Total: 15 min including a 1-min break between rounds. Sustainable pace — she should be breathing hard but not gassed.

---

## Day 4 (Upper B) — Hard Conditioning Day (High Intent)

This is her one "hard" session of the week. Lower body is fresh from a rest day.

**Format:** 30/30 intervals, 15 minutes total (15 rounds).

Alternate two movements:
- **Odd rounds:** Burpees (max effort)
- **Even rounds:** Squat jumps OR fast skater jumps

Push close to max each 30-sec block. This is the one she should finish properly winded.

---

## Day 5 (Lower B) — Steady-State / Zone 2 (Easy)

After Nordics and pistols, hard intervals would compromise recovery into the weekend. Keep it aerobic.

15 min continuous, choose one:
- **Shadowboxing** — 3-min rounds, 30-sec rest, light footwork
- **Hotel hallway walk-jog** — easy jog 1 min, walk 1 min
- **Mat flow:** continuous low-intensity movement — inchworms, bear crawls, lateral shuffles, mountain climbers at conversational pace

Nasal breathing if she can hold it. Heart rate ~60–70% max. This aids recovery rather than taxing it.

---

## Week 2 Progression

Same template, slight bump:
- **Day 1 EMOM:** Add 5 reps to jump squats and lunges, or compress to 50-sec windows
- **Day 2 circuit:** 45/15 instead of 40/20
- **Day 4 intervals:** Add 1 round (16 total, 16 min)
- **Day 5 Zone 2:** Stays the same — easy is easy

---

## Watch-Outs

- **Day 4 is the only true high-intent session.** If she's jet-lagged, slept poorly, or under-eaten, swap it for the Day 2 circuit format. Don't stack hard conditioning on a depleted athlete in a maintenance block — that's where muscle loss creeps in.
- **Total hard cardio = 2 sessions/week max.** More than that during low-stimulus lifting and she'll start eating into the muscle we're protecting.
- **Fuel the finishers.** Add ~20–30g carbs pre-session if she's training in a fasted state — particularly on Day 4.
- **If she's loving it and wants more,** the answer is "save it for when you're back and we're not trying to maintain in a deficit-prone environment." Conditioning appetite is great fuel for the Week 7–12 block.

Ready for the return block when you are.

# Travel Day Eating — Keep It Simple

The whole game on travel days is **hit protein, don't undereat, don't overthink it.** Restaurant and room service menus make protein easy if you know what to order.

---

## Daily Targets

- **Protein:** 1.6–2.0 g/kg bodyweight — this is the non-negotiable. For most women her size, that's ~110–140g/day.
- **Calories:** Maintenance. Not a deficit. Under-eating during a low-stimulus block accelerates muscle loss.
- **Carbs & fat:** Fill the rest of the calories around the protein anchor. Don't fear either.
- **Water:** 2.5–3L. Add 500ml per flight hour.

Simplest rule: **palm of protein at every meal + a snack with protein.** That's it.

---

## The Order-Anywhere Playbook

### Breakfast (room service or hotel buffet)
- **3-egg omelette** + side of fruit + whole grain toast
- **Greek yogurt + berries + granola** (buffet staple)
- **Smoked salmon + eggs** if it's on the menu — top tier
- Avoid: pastry-only breakfasts, "continental" plates with no protein

### Lunch (restaurant or grab-and-go)
- **Grilled chicken salad** — ask for double chicken, dressing on the side
- **Salmon or steak + vegetables + rice or potato**
- **Burrito bowl** style — protein, beans, rice, veg, skip the chips
- **Sushi** — sashimi-heavy, plus a roll
- Sandwich shops: turkey/chicken/tuna, double the meat

### Dinner (restaurant)
- **Steak / chicken / fish + two sides** (one veg, one carb) — works in any cuisine
- **Asian:** stir-fry with extra protein, skip sweet sauces if she's watching calories
- **Italian:** grilled fish or chicken main, not pasta-as-main. If pasta, ask for added chicken/shrimp.
- **Burger** is fine — pick one with veg, eat the bun or don't, her call

### Snacks (keep in her bag/room)
- Beef jerky or biltong
- Protein bar (aim for 20g+ protein, <10g sugar — Barebells, Built, RXBar)
- Greek yogurt cups (mini-bar or grab from a shop)
- Mixed nuts + a piece of fruit
- Single-serve protein powder sachets + shaker — bulletproof backup

---

## The "Bad Day" Protocol

When she's stuck in an airport, in back-to-back meetings, or the only option is a service station:

1. **Buy a protein source first** — jerky, a protein shake, a chicken wrap, hard-boiled eggs from a fridge
2. **Then add carbs** — banana, rice cake, sandwich
3. **Don't skip the meal.** Skipped meals are where the deficit creeps in.

A mediocre meal that hits 30g protein beats a "perfect" meal she didn't eat.

---

## Around Training

- **Pre-session:** something with carbs + a bit of protein 60–90 min before. Banana + Greek yogurt, or a protein bar. Not essential but helps the Day 4 finisher.
- **Post-session:** protein within ~2 hours. Real meal preferred; shake if no meal is coming soon.

---

## Alcohol

Realistic answer: 1–2 drinks on a given evening won't derail her. More than that on multiple nights *will* — it suppresses recovery, protein synthesis, and sleep quality, which is exactly the trifecta we're trying to protect in a maintenance block. If she's out client-entertaining, coach her toward spirits + soda over beer/wine, and to front-load protein at dinner.

---

## The One-Line Version for Her

> "Protein at every meal, don't skip meals, drink water, and don't stress the rest."

That'll get her through two weeks intact. Want me to put the whole 2-week plan — training, finishers, nutrition — into a single client-facing handout?

# Tracking a Hold Block — What to Measure

The instinct on a maintenance block is to track the same things as a growth block (weights, reps, weight on the scale) — but those are the wrong metrics here. They'll either falsely signal regression or pressure her to push harder than the block calls for.

**The goal of tracking on a hold block is to confirm she's holding, not to chase progress.** Pick metrics that go *flat* when things are going well.

---

## The Recommended Metric: Daily Check-In Score (1–5)

One number per day, logged in her notes app. Takes 30 seconds. Average it weekly.

Each morning she rates:

1. **Sleep quality** (1–5)
2. **Energy** (1–5)
3. **Training quality** — only on training days (1–5)
4. **Nutrition adherence** — did she hit protein + meals? (1–5)

**Weekly average target: 3.5+**

This is the right metric because it captures the things that actually determine whether she holds muscle — recovery, fuel, training proximity — without being something she can "win" by overreaching. A flat or stable weekly average means the plan is working.

---

## Supporting Metrics (Pick 1–2, Not All)

### Performance anchors — measured once per week, not per session

- **Pull-up AMRAP on Day 1** — same time of day, same conditions. Target: hold within 1 rep of her Week 6 number.
- **Bulgarian split squat reps at 3-sec tempo** — same target.

If these hold, she's holding. That's it. No need for more.

### Body metric — optional

- **Waist measurement, once per week, morning, fasted.** Not weight. Scale weight fluctuates wildly with travel (sodium, fibre, sleep, hydration) and will spook her. Waist is more stable and more meaningful.

---

## What NOT to Track

- **Daily scale weight** — too noisy on travel, emotionally counterproductive
- **Calories** — adherence to the "protein + don't skip meals" rule is enough; calorie counting on restaurant food is guesswork that breeds anxiety
- **Steps as a performance metric** — fine as a habit cue, but don't let her treat 12k step days as "making up" for anything
- **Session-to-session PRs** — wrong block for it

---

## The Reframe to Give Her

> "On a hold block, **flat is the win.** If your weekly check-in average is 3.5+, your pull-up number holds, and your waist is stable, you've done the job. You haven't backslid — you've protected the work."

The trip isn't a pause in her programme. It's a deliberate phase with its own success criteria. Tracking the right things makes that real for her.

---

## Optional: Weekly Check-In to You

Have her send you, end of each week:
- Average daily score
- Pull-up AMRAP number
- One sentence: "What was hard this week?"

That's all you need to know whether to greenlight Week 7 or adjust the return.

Want me to package the whole thing — programme, finishers, nutrition, tracking — into a one-page client handout?

# Day 4 Active Rest Swap — Week 1

Good instinct pulling her off the hard session rather than forcing it. Day 4 is the high-intent conditioning day plus a full upper session — exactly the wrong session to grind through when she's already depleted. Skipping entirely is fine, but active rest is better: it preserves the routine, supports recovery, and avoids the psychological "I missed a session" spiral.

---

## The Swap: 30–40 min Restorative Session

### Block 1 — Easy Movement (15 min)

Pick one, conversational pace, nasal breathing throughout:

- **Walk** outside or hotel hallway/treadmill
- **Easy mat flow** — inchworms, world's greatest stretch, cat-cow, 90/90 transitions, bear crawl, repeat
- **Shadowboxing** at very light intent

Heart rate stays low. She should be able to hold a full conversation.

---

### Block 2 — Mobility Flow (15 min)

Slow, controlled, no intensity. Two rounds of:

| Movement | Duration |
|---|---|
| Cat-cow | 60 sec |
| World's greatest stretch | 45 sec/side |
| 90/90 hip switches | 60 sec |
| Thoracic openers (side-lying) | 45 sec/side |
| Couch stretch | 45 sec/side |
| Child's pose with reach | 60 sec |
| Deep squat hold + reach | 60 sec |

---

### Block 3 — Light Activation (Optional, 5–10 min)

Only if she feels good after the first two blocks. Wakes the nervous system without taxing recovery:

- Dead bugs 2 x 8/side
- Glute bridges 2 x 12 (no hold)
- Scapular pulls on the bar 2 x 8
- Band pull-aparts or towel face pulls 2 x 12

Stop immediately if she's not feeling better than when she started.

---

## What She Should NOT Do

- **No finisher.** Skip the Day 4 conditioning entirely. The whole point is to drop intent.
- **No "make-up" session later in the week.** The volume is gone, that's fine. Hold blocks tolerate this easily.
- **No pull-ups, no push-ups to failure.** Don't sneak in "just one set" — that defeats the purpose.

---

## Rest of the Week Adjustment

- **Day 5 (Lower B):** Run as planned *if* she wakes up feeling restored. If still flat, push it to Day 6 and take another full rest day.
- **Don't add the missed Day 4 session anywhere.** Lost volume on a hold block is a non-issue. Lost recovery is the actual risk.
- **Log it in her daily check-in.** A tired Day 4 in Week 1 is useful data — if it repeats in Week 2, we look at sleep, food, or travel load, not training.

---

## The Message to Her

> "Taking active rest when you're tired isn't backsliding — it's the block working as designed. Hold blocks are built to absorb days like this. Move easy today, sleep well tonight, and pick up Day 5 when you feel ready."

Fatigue mid-trip is expected. Building the option in ahead of time means she uses it without guilt, which is exactly what you want.

# Pushing Back — Briefly

Before I write this, I want to flag the tension: she's nervous about losing muscle, but the actual risk to her muscle isn't undertraining — it's **overreaching while under-recovered on the road**. She already needed an active rest day in Week 1. Adding intensity on top of travel fatigue, restaurant food, and disrupted sleep is the thing most likely to cause the outcome she's afraid of.

**The original Week 2 already progresses.** Tempo creeps, holds get longer, 1.5-rep variants appear, finishers add volume. It's calibrated.

That said — her nervous system matters too. If she *feels* like she's holding, she'll eat better, sleep better, and return to Week 7 in better shape than if she spends two weeks anxious about backsliding. So let's give her a Week 2 that **feels harder without actually adding recovery cost.** Perceived progression, same physiological load.

---

## Week 2 — Adjusted for Perceived Progression

### What Changes (Feel)

- **New movement variants** on each day — novelty reads as progress
- **One measurable "test" rep** per session she can log and beat
- **Density tweaks** — slightly shorter rest, same volume
- **Tempo and pause changes** that are felt clearly in the muscle

### What Doesn't Change (Recovery Cost)

- Total sets per muscle group
- Number of hard sessions
- Proximity to failure (still 0–2 RIR)
- Finisher hard-day count (still 1)

---

## Session-by-Session Adjustments

### Day 1 — Upper A

| Original | Week 2 Version |

| Pull-ups 4 x AMRAP | **Pull-ups 4 x AMRAP + 5-sec top hold on final rep** — log the AMRAP number |
| Pike push-ups 3 x 8–12 | **Deficit pike push-ups** (hands on books/towels) 3 x 8–10 |
| Archer push-ups 3 x 6–8/side | **Archer push-ups with 2-sec pause at bottom** 3 x 6–8/side |
| Inverted rows / scapular pulls 3 x 10–12 | Same, **add 1-sec squeeze at top** |
| Hollow body hold 3 x 30 sec | **Hollow body hold 3 x 40 sec** |

**Test rep:** Pull-up AMRAP set 1. Log it. Target: match Week 1.

---

### Day 2 — Lower A

| Original | Week 2 Version |
|---|---|
| Bulgarian split squat 4 x 10–12/leg, 3-sec descent | **1.5-rep Bulgarian split squat** 3 x 8/leg, 3-sec descent |
| Single-leg RDL 3 x 10/leg | Same, **+2-sec pause at bottom stretch** |
| Cossack squat 3 x 8/side | **Cossack squat with 3-sec pause at bottom** 3 x 6/side |
| Glute bridge march 3 x 10/side | **Single-leg glute bridge with 3-sec hold at top** 3 x 10/leg |
| Copenhagen plank 2 x 20 sec/side | **Copenhagen plank 2 x 25 sec/side** |

**Test rep:** Bulgarian split squat reps at tempo, lead leg. Log it.

---

### Day 4 — Upper B

| Original | Week 2 Version |
|---|---|
| Chin-ups 4 x AMRAP | **Chin-ups 3 x AMRAP + 1 set of 5-sec eccentrics x 5 reps** |
| Push-ups, 2-sec pause 4 x 12–15 | **Push-ups, 3-sec descent + 2-sec pause** 4 x 10–12 |
| Pseudo planche push-ups 3 x 6–8 | Same, **+1-sec pause at bottom** |
| Towel face pulls 3 x 15 | Same, **+2-sec hold at end range** |
| Side plank reach-through 3 x 8/side | **Side plank reach-through 3 x 10/side** |

**Note:** If Day 4 fatigue repeats from Week 1, run the active rest swap again. Do not force this session.

---

### Day 5 — Lower B

| Original | Week 2 Version |
|---|---|
| Pistol progression 4 x 6–8/leg | **Pistol progression with 3-sec descent** 3 x 5–6/leg |
| Reverse lunge 3 x 10/leg | **Walking reverse lunge with pause at bottom** 3 x 8/leg |
| Nordic curl negatives 3 x 4–6 | **Nordic negatives, 6-sec descent** 3 x 4–5 |
| Single-leg glute bridge 3 x 12/leg, 2-sec hold | Same, **3-sec hold** |
| Calf raise 4 x 15–20 | **Single-leg calf raise with 2-sec stretch pause** 4 x 12–15 |

**Test rep:** Nordic negative descent time. Target a clean 6 seconds.

---

## Finisher Adjustment

Keep the Week 2 finisher progression I gave you earlier — those bumps are already baked in. **Do not add another layer.** That's where this tips into overreaching.

---

## The "Progression Log" for Her

Give her three numbers to track across Week 2:

1. **Day 1: Pull-up AMRAP, set 1**
2. **Day 2: Bulgarian split squat reps at tempo, lead leg**
3. **Day 5: Nordic negative controlled descent time**

If any of these *match or beat* Week 1, that's objective evidence she's holding or gaining. Hold blocks often produce small strength gains from movement quality work, even without loading — she should see at least one of these tick up.

---

## The Message to Her

> "Week 2 is harder on purpose — slower tempos, longer holds, tougher variants. If your three test numbers hold or improve, you're not just maintaining, you're refining. That's progress you carry back into Week 7."

This gives her the felt sense of pushing forward without the recovery cost that would actually threaten what she's trying to protect.

One more thing — if her Day 1 Week 2 pull-up number drops by 2+ reps from Week 1, that's the signal she's accumulating fatigue, not progressing. Pull intensity back immediately. Don't let her grind through it.

# 2-Week Travel Plan — At a Glance

**Client:** 32F, intermediate, mid-hypertrophy block (Week 6 → return at Week 7)
**Equipment:** Yoga mat, doorway pull-up bar
**Goal:** Hold muscle, return ready to resume loading

---

## Weekly Structure (Both Weeks)

| Day | Session |
|---|---|
| 1 | Upper A + finisher |
| 2 | Lower A + finisher |
| 3 | Mobility flow + core (optional) |
| 4 | Upper B + finisher *(active rest if depleted)* |
| 5 | Lower B + finisher |
| 6–7 | Rest / walking |

---

## Training — Week 1 vs Week 2

### Day 1 — Upper A

| Exercise | Week 1 | Week 2 |
|---|---|---|
| Pull-ups | 4 x AMRAP (1 RIR) | 4 x AMRAP + 5-sec top hold final rep |
| Pike push-ups | 3 x 8–12 | **Deficit** pike push-ups 3 x 8–10 |
| Archer push-ups | 3 x 6–8/side | Same + **2-sec pause at bottom** |
| Inverted rows / scap pulls | 3 x 10–12 | Same + 1-sec top squeeze |
| Hollow body hold | 3 x 30 sec | 3 x 40 sec |

**Test rep:** Pull-up AMRAP set 1

---

### Day 2 — Lower A

| Exercise | Week 1 | Week 2 |
|---|---|---|
| Bulgarian split squat | 4 x 10–12/leg, 3-sec descent | **1.5-rep style** 3 x 8/leg, 3-sec descent |
| Single-leg RDL | 3 x 10/leg | Same + 2-sec pause at stretch |
| Cossack squat | 3 x 8/side | 3 x 6/side + 3-sec bottom pause |
| Glute bridge march | 3 x 10/side | **Single-leg** glute bridge 3 x 10/leg + 3-sec top hold |

**Test rep:** Bulgarian split squat reps at tempo, lead leg

---

10 min flow (cat-cow → world's greatest stretch → 90/90 → thoracic openers) + hollow hold 3 x 30s + side plank 2 x 30s/side. Same both weeks.

| Exercise | Week 1 | Week 2 |
|---|---|---|
| Chin-ups | 4 x AMRAP (1 RIR) | 3 x AMRAP + 1 x 5 reps, 5-sec eccentrics |
| Push-ups | 4 x 12–15, 2-sec pause | 4 x 10–12, **3-sec descent + 2-sec pause** |
| Pseudo planche push-ups | 3 x 6–8 | Same + 1-sec bottom pause |
| Towel face pulls | 3 x 15 | Same + 2-sec end-range hold |
| Side plank reach-through | 3 x 8/side | 3 x 10/side |

*If she's depleted (as in Week 1): swap for active rest — 15 min easy movement, 15 min mobility flow, optional 5–10 min light activation. No finisher.*

---

| Exercise | Week 1 | Week 2 |
|---|---|---|
| Pistol progression | 4 x 6–8/leg | 3 x 5–6/leg, **3-sec descent** |
| Reverse lunge | 3 x 10/leg | **Walking** reverse lunge 3 x 8/leg + bottom pause |
| Nordic curl negatives | 3 x 4–6 | 3 x 4–5, **6-sec descent** |
| Single-leg glute bridge | 3 x 12/leg, 2-sec hold | Same, **3-sec hold** |
| Calf raise | 4 x 15–20 | **Single-leg** 4 x 12–15 + 2-sec stretch pause |

**Test rep:** Nordic negative descent time (target clean 6 sec)

| Day | Format | Week 1 | Week 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Day 1 | EMOM lower (jump squats / high knees / reverse lunges) | 5 rounds, 15 min | +5 reps each, or 50-sec windows |
| Day 2 | Upper/core circuit, 3 rounds | 40/20 work-rest | 45/15 work-rest |
| Day 4 | **Hard 30/30 intervals** (burpees / squat jumps) | 15 rounds, 15 min | 16 rounds, 16 min |
| Day 5 | **Zone 2** — shadowbox / walk-jog / mat flow | 15 min, nasal breathing | Same |

Day 4 is the only true high-intent session of the week. Skip it if depleted.

---

## Equipment Opportunism

If hotel gym has dumbbells, slot them in **without changing the plan**:

- **Lower:** Load Bulgarian split squats (best use), single-leg RDLs, reverse lunges
- **Upper bonus (3 sets each, 1 RIR):** Lateral raises 12–15, curls 10–12, overhead tricep extension 10–12
- **Rule:** Don't chase load. Don't add anything she'd lose access to the next day.

---

## Nutrition — The One-Liner

> "Protein at every meal, don't skip meals, drink water, don't stress the rest."

- **Protein:** 1.6–2.0 g/kg (palm at every meal)
- **Calories:** Maintenance, not deficit
- **Snacks to keep on hand:** Jerky, protein bars, Greek yogurt, nuts, protein powder sachets
- **Bad day protocol:** Buy protein first, add carbs second, never skip
- **Alcohol:** 1–2 drinks fine; spirits + soda over beer/wine; front-load protein

---

## Tracking — Daily Check-In (1–5 each)

1. Sleep quality
2. Energy
3. Training quality (training days only)
4. Nutrition adherence

**Weekly target average: 3.5+**

Plus three weekly performance anchors — Pull-up AMRAP (Day 1), Bulgarian split squat reps at tempo (Day 2), Nordic descent time (Day 5). **Hold or beat Week 1 = job done.**

Optional: waist measurement once weekly, fasted. **No daily scale.**

---

## Decision Rules

| Signal | Action |
|---|---|
| Tired on a lifting day | Run active rest template, don't make up the session |
| Day 4 fatigue repeats Week 2 | Run active rest again, no guilt |
| Pull-up AMRAP drops 2+ reps in Week 2 | Pull intensity back immediately — fatigue accumulating |
| Daily check-in average <3 for 3+ days | Message you, consider dropping a session |
| Hotel gym has dumbbells | Slot in lower-body loading + bonus arms/delts |
| No hotel gym | Plan runs exactly as written, no compromise |

---

## End-of-Week Report to You

Each Sunday she sends:
- Weekly check-in average
- Three test-rep numbers
- One sentence: "What was hard this week?"

That's enough to greenlight Week 7 or adjust the return.

---

**Bottom line:** Week 1 grooves the stimulus, Week 2 sharpens it through tempo and variant difficulty without raising recovery cost. Flat performance = success. She returns at Week 7 with one deload session, then resumes normal loading.

Ready to build the Week 7–12 return block whenever you are.

# 2-Week Travel Plan — At a Glance

**Client:** 32F, intermediate, mid-hypertrophy block (Week 6 → return at Week 7)
**Equipment:** Yoga mat, doorway pull-up bar
**Goal:** Hold muscle, return ready to resume loading

---

## Weekly Structure (Both Weeks)

| Day | Session |
|---|---|
| 1 | Upper A + finisher |
| 2 | Lower A + finisher |
| 3 | Mobility flow + core (optional) |
| 4 | Upper B + finisher *(active rest if depleted)* |
| 5 | Lower B + finisher |
| 6–7 | Rest / walking |

---

## Training — Week 1 vs Week 2

### Day 1 — Upper A

| Exercise | Week 1 | Week 2 |
|---|---|---|
| Pull-ups | 4 x AMRAP (1 RIR) | 4 x AMRAP + 5-sec top hold final rep |
| Pike push-ups | 3 x 8–12 | **Deficit** pike push-ups 3 x 8–10 |
| Archer push-ups | 3 x 6–8/side | Same + **2-sec pause at bottom** |
| Inverted rows / scap pulls | 3 x 10–12 | Same + 1-sec top squeeze |
| Hollow body hold | 3 x 30 sec | 3 x 40 sec |

**Test rep:** Pull-up AMRAP set 1

---

### Day 2 — Lower A

| Exercise | Week 1 | Week 2 |
|---|---|---|
| Bulgarian split squat | 4 x 10–12/leg, 3-sec descent | **1.5-rep style** 3 x 8/leg, 3-sec descent |
| Single-leg RDL | 3 x 10/leg | Same + 2-sec pause at stretch |
| Cossack squat | 3 x 8/side | 3 x 6/side + 3-sec bottom pause |
| Glute bridge march | 3 x 10/side | **Single-leg** glute bridge 3 x 10/leg + 3-sec top hold |
| Copenhagen plank | 2 x 20 sec/side | 2 x 25 sec/side |

**Test rep:** Bulgarian split squat reps at tempo, lead leg

---

### Day 3 — Mobility + Core (optional)

10 min flow (cat-cow → world's greatest stretch → 90/90 → thoracic openers) + hollow hold 3 x 30s + side plank 2 x 30s/side. Same both weeks.

---

### Day 4 — Upper B

| Exercise | Week 1 | Week 2 |
|---|---|---|
| Chin-ups | 4 x AMRAP (1 RIR) | 3 x AMRAP + 1 x 5 reps, 5-sec eccentrics |
| Push-ups | 4 x 12–15, 2-sec pause | 4 x 10–12, **3-sec descent + 2-sec pause** |
| Pseudo planche push-ups | 3 x 6–8 | Same + 1-sec bottom pause |
| Towel face pulls | 3 x 15 | Same + 2-sec end-range hold |
| Side plank reach-through | 3 x 8/side | 3 x 10/side |

*If she's depleted (as in Week 1): swap for active rest — 15 min easy movement, 15 min mobility flow, optional 5–10 min light activation. No finisher.*

---

### Day 5 — Lower B

| Exercise | Week 1 | Week 2 |
|---|---|---|
| Pistol progression | 4 x 6–8/leg | 3 x 5–6/leg, **3-sec descent** |
| Reverse lunge | 3 x 10/leg | **Walking** reverse lunge 3 x 8/leg + bottom pause |
| Nordic curl negatives | 3 x 4–6 | 3 x 4–5, **6-sec descent** |
| Single-leg glute bridge | 3 x 12/leg, 2-sec hold | Same, **3-sec hold** |
| Calf raise | 4 x 15–20 | **Single-leg** 4 x 12–15 + 2-sec stretch pause |

**Test rep:** Nordic negative descent time (target clean 6 sec)

---

## Cardio Finishers (15 min, post-session)

| Day | Format | Week 1 | Week 2 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Day 1 | EMOM lower (jump squats / high knees / reverse lunges) | 5 rounds, 15 min | +5 reps each, or 50-sec windows |
| Day 2 | Upper/core circuit, 3 rounds | 40/20 work-rest | 45/15 work-rest |
| Day 4 | **Hard 30/30 intervals** (burpees / squat jumps) | 15 rounds, 15 min | 16 rounds, 16 min |
| Day 5 | **Zone 2** — shadowbox / walk-jog / mat flow | 15 min, nasal breathing | Same |

Day 4 is the only true high-intent session of the week. Skip it if depleted.

---

## Equipment Opportunism

If hotel gym has dumbbells, slot them in **without changing the plan**:

- **Lower:** Load Bulgarian split squats (best use), single-leg RDLs, reverse lunges
- **Upper bonus (3 sets each, 1 RIR):** Lateral raises 12–15, curls 10–12, overhead tricep extension 10–12
- **Rule:** Don't chase load. Don't add anything she'd lose access to the next day.

---

## Nutrition — The One-Liner

> "Protein at every meal, don't skip meals, drink water, don't stress the rest."

- **Protein:** 1.6–2.0 g/kg (palm at every meal)
- **Calories:** Maintenance, not deficit
- **Snacks to keep on hand:** Jerky, protein bars, Greek yogurt, nuts, protein powder sachets
- **Bad day protocol:** Buy protein first, add carbs second, never skip
- **Alcohol:** 1–2 drinks fine; spirits + soda over beer/wine; front-load protein

---

## Tracking — Daily Check-In (1–5 each)

1. Sleep quality
2. Energy
3. Training quality (training days only)
4. Nutrition adherence

**Weekly target average: 3.5+**

Plus three weekly performance anchors — Pull-up AMRAP (Day 1), Bulgarian split squat reps at tempo (Day 2), Nordic descent time (Day 5). **Hold or beat Week 1 = job done.**

Optional: waist measurement once weekly, fasted. **No daily scale.**

---

## Decision Rules

| Signal | Action |
|---|---|
| Tired on a lifting day | Run active rest template, don't make up the session |
| Day 4 fatigue repeats Week 2 | Run active rest again, no guilt |
| Pull-up AMRAP drops 2+ reps in Week 2 | Pull intensity back immediately — fatigue accumulating |
| Daily check-in average <3 for 3+ days | Message you, consider dropping a session |
| Hotel gym has dumbbells | Slot in lower-body loading + bonus arms/delts |
| No hotel gym | Plan runs exactly as written, no compromise |

---

## End-of-Week Report to You

Each Sunday she sends:
- Weekly check-in average
- Three test-rep numbers
- One sentence: "What was hard this week?"

That's enough to greenlight Week 7 or adjust the return.

---

**Bottom line:** Week 1 grooves the stimulus, Week 2 sharpens it through tempo and variant difficulty without raising recovery cost. Flat performance = success. She returns at Week 7 with one deload session, then resumes normal loading.

Ready to build the Week 7–12 return block whenever you are.
